title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-04-12
lineage: [SBD > Reel master > Sonic Solutions > DAT ] + [Aud > cassette master > PCM > DAT > Sonic Solutions] > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1970 show highlighted by an epic “Dancin’ in the Streets” and fiery Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The SBD recording is remarkably clean – most reviewers praise its crisp, well‑balanced mix (aside from a few complained three‑second gaps between tracks). Musically the concert shines with a blistering “Dancin’ in the Streets”, a scorching Viola Lee Blues, and tight renditions of Deep Elem, Black Peter and Man’s World. The set flows smoothly, especially the Candyman → Viola Lee transition, though the China→Rider segue is noted as weak.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the performance 4‑5 stars and describe the recording as crystal clear; only a handful of low‑star outliers mention minor edits or gaps, giving an overall strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with good instrument separation; a few reviewers note annoying three‑second pauses between tracks and minor patch‑mix quirks, but no major dropouts or distortion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert rides a strong groove, with smooth transitions (notably Candyman → Viola Lee) and an overall cohesive feel; only the China→Rider transition is described as sloppy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers call his guitar work on “Dancin’” snaky, peak‑season, and uniquely inventive.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass is praised for driving the jams (especially during Dancin' and the drum break).
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ gets prominent, “magical” treatment on Viola Lee Blues and adds weight to Dancin’.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum jam receives high marks as a highlight; Bill’s playing is described as solid and propulsive.
